newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania shares gain slightly, volume still low.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania shares gain slightly, volume still low.

text.p: Lithuanian shares made a slight gain on Friday but volumes remained low, dealers said.
The group A index inched up by 9.72 points to 2,408.02 in lacklustre central market trade of 751,000 litas.
Gains are seen on the horizon but dealers say the bourse is not set for a bull-run like last month's, when shares soared steeply to new highs.
"There is some profit taking right now among some blue-chip holers," one dealer said.
But dealers say that most blue chip stocks are now good value and won't fall much further, if at all.
"Prices in general have reached their lowest level," said one broker.
But investors are still waiting for more news on shares like Lithuania Gas and the Lithuanian Sea Shipping Company.
"Those shares are quite cheap now, but investors want to see if the government is serious about selling off its majority stake in both companies," he added.
Ukio Bank was Friday's biggest blue chip jump, rising 9.99 percent to 20.91 litas in trade of 48,500 litas. Nomura said earlier this year that Ukio was a good equity investment.
Akmenas cementas also advanced, rising 7.14 percent to 1.50 litas. Only 1,500 litas worth of its shares were swapped.
Kalnapilis lost ground, falling 9.97 percent to 6.14 litas in trade of 33,000 litas.
Birzai Milk also lost ground, declining five percent to 7.60 litas. Block trades reached 286,000 litas on Friday.
Investors continued to show little appetite for Lithuanian debt, with the secondary T-bill market turning over just 95,630 litas.
